content: **Server guidelines and house rules for all Tales from Arcania events.**

Hateful language will not be tolerated. We want to be inclusive to all our players and make them feel welcome. Any language that is disrespectful towards anyone based on their religion, politics, skin color, sexuality, etc etc will not be tolerated.
In conflicts between players (not to be confused with the conflict between player characters which can be a part of story arc, and shouldn’t be taken personally) do your best to be kind, courteous and helpful. This style of gaming is very dependent on interpersonal relations, and a sour note will resonate throughout the server. We recognize that many are going through tough times here. It is better to see our game as a haven from the real world, to be a place where you can deal with your anxieties and frustrations in a healthy, mutually consensual way. Hate language will not be tolerated.

Beyond just your inventory, there is an honor system between player actions and DM intent. If we have made a mistake and left an exploitable loophole, please tell us so that we can rectify it. Additionally, if you suspect that the DM’s may have made a mistake bring it to us in private through direct message. Don’t point out the mistake for others to exploit.

A short rest takes an actual hour. A long rest is typically taken when you leave the server for the day and is meant to represent an actual long rest. In other words, we have a built in mechanic to help you take time off of the server. This game will cause many to invest deeply in their character. Don’t allow fear of missing out on the game to cause you to miss out on taking care of your life and your mental health. This both a server rule, and a house rule.

Welcome to Season Four of Tales from Arcania. 
Whether you are a seasoned vet with us, or you have no clue what we are all about the channels in the things you should read category are here to help you get started. @ a mod to get your player tag. You are responsible for understanding our server rules and house rules before you interact with any other part of the server.

Ah, meta gaming. That age old pastime of players. To the experienced player, it is the sharing of tricks of the trade and the fear of sub optimal playing. An experienced player will also relish the value of making intentionally unreliable or intentionally against the grain choices for role play reasons. 

But to the newer player, there comes a perceived pressure when their decisions are sub optimal.  Wisdom is in being gentle enough with your opinions about how they should play, be it mechanics or social decisions. 

Personally, I often have a hard time reading social cues. And even then, lots of us have been playing together for years and ride that wave of emphatic group opinion. 
The number of neurodivergent players on the server is above half. And that is something to consider when it comes to interplay discussions about the how tos of role playing.

Meta gaming and theory crafting about the plot is some of the most gratifying things a dm can read. But its is an acquired rhythm that becomes available as your become more experienced. There are lots of kick ass players on this server. There are also lots of people who love to protect and nurture those who could use it among us.

Rhetoric has come to mean pompous. Which is completely wrong. Rhetoric is Aristotle's discussion of how to deliver information to people. The five cannons of the field of rhetoric are: invention, arrangement, style, memory, and delivery.

The way you speak is wonderful. Your audience is not. Your audience is on a similar bell curve as all of the rest of humanity as it applies to how they communicate. From the eloquent to the inarticulate, there is an unknowable average. However, your issue is not with how articulate you are. It is how your audience receives information that may be the stumbling block here.
If so, the Rhetoric cannons 3 and 5 (arrangement and delivery) might be of some use. A person whose learning style is visual and not auditory might just be expressing frustration. They here some one well spoken, but their learning style does not match your teaching style. 

The cannon of arrangement charges us with the duty of understanding our audience. Understand that they might be just as confused as your are as to why they are not understanding the information you are providing. A visual learner needs pictures. Which you are in no way required to provide, nor am I encouraging you to change what you are doing. But I have heard your complaints on several occasions, and I am hoping this might help bring some clarity.

Most of the feed back was positive. The negative points mainly came from players who felt that they had a lack of player agency when we had to make corrections. From a top down perspective my reaction to the issues I watched as well as player feed back can be found in the new server rules. I won't post direct text here from any particular player, because that feels somewhat inappropriate. There were some complaints of favoritism and nepotism, as well as long wait times during combat. As well as some hard feeling from a couple of the players who we had to call out. Some of this is us, which is one of the reasons I asked for so many dms for next year. DM burn out is a real thing in roanoke. But some of it was also players failing to take personal responsibility for their attitudes and actions. We didn't ask anyone to leave this year when maybe we should have. It's always been my goal to try and retain people with kindness.

What went wrong is something I've thought about often, some of my character flaws involve being blunt and wanting to fix things as soon as I perceive there to be a danger, or a situation that could end up hurting others. But on the other side of that coin, I find my self analyzing my self for faults when the folks who are doing the negative things sometimes do not.  Try to remember that though we are running a public server this is also a free service. We are volunteers giving our time in a labor of love. When that labor is met with petty squabbles, bitterness and resentment it can be tough to stay humble and keep serving. People can sometimes find themselves caught in despair or attitudes of entitlement and forget that the events happen daily because we are playing a game that tells a complete story. Sometimes they forget that this isn't a single player experience and that their characters reactions are also a player choice. And sometimes we need to remember that people are concerned about their reputation. Which is a valid concern. We are weighing between likely consequences of taking steps to intervene and the consequences of our inaction in a case by case string of choices.
